attribution.note: Marcus wrote this aside in his own Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The drafter kept the 'appears' qualifier, and the proposition matches his words. The domain-difference point uses 'may' and is fairly left out. This is a hedged observation, not a firm assertion of fact.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats 'appears' as a tentative impression, and 'heavily' has no stated measure. Declining to score is fair. Scoring would mean reading his words as a firm claim about actual training reliance, which is stronger than what he said.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own launch disclosure, available on the stated date. It describes RL training of the chain of thought but says nothing about how much synthetic data was used. It is context only.

reviews.rationale: Marcus said only that o1 'appears' to depend heavily on synthetic data. That is a hedged impression with no measure of 'heavily', so it is not a firm commitment that can be scored. The only evidence, OpenAI's launch post, describes reinforcement learning and is silent on how much synthetic data was used, so it would not settle the question even under a firm reading. Not adjudicable.
